function.mechanism: Acidifies food and, in its undissociated form, disrupts microbial growth by intracellular acidification and metabolic inhibition.

adi.basis: ADI not considered necessary / historically not specified for acetic acid and salts (SCF; reaffirmed in EFSA context including 2013 citation in EFSA 2022 opinion).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded no safety concern for buffered vinegar at proposed maximum/typical use levels; for acetic acid oral intake EFSA references ADI not necessary.

adi.basis: Group ADI not limited for acetic acid and potassium/sodium salts (17th meeting, maintained at 49th meeting); current entry also states no safety concern at current levels for flavouring-agent use.

concerns.summary: A 2026 prospective cohort (NutriNet-Sante) reported an association between higher acetic-acid preservative intake and overall cancer incidence (HR 1.12, 95% CI 1.01-1.25); causality was not established.
Concentrated or massive ingestion can cause severe corrosive/systemic toxicity (including reported multiorgan failure and fatal case reports).

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2022: no safety concern for buffered vinegar at proposed maximum/typical use levels.
EFSA reference context: ADI for acetic acid oral intake not considered necessary.
JECFA: group ADI not limited for acetic acid and sodium/potassium salts.
FDA: acetic acid affirmed as GRAS under 21 CFR 184.1005 when used under GMP.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric ADI applies in EFSA/JECFA assessments (not necessary/not limited), so classic ADI exceedance is not the primary risk metric; highest modeled exposures occur in young children.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory consensus supports low concern at intended use levels (GRAS/approved; ADI not necessary or not limited), but recent observational epidemiology and known high-dose corrosive toxicity argue against classifying as risk_free.
key_factors: EU authorization and EFSA no-safety-concern conclusion at proposed use levels
FDA GRAS affirmation with GMP and use conditions
JECFA group ADI not limited history
Recent cohort association signal requiring follow-up
Concentration-dependent corrosive toxicity at high exposures
